1,Lifting Rod, a short rod (typically wood) for probing and lifting latches.
1,Screwdriver, for turning screws when so needed. Come in multiple sizes.
1,Hacksaw, a small saw able to cut through all but the strongest metals given the time.
1,Files, used to trim bits of wood and metal can quietly widen holes and cut-away bars.
1,Pliers, plain old pliers with multiple uses for working nuts and screws.
1,Wire Cutter, a plier-like tool able to quickly cut a wire.
1,Magnifying lens, for peaking into small hard to see spots (such as a key hole)
1,Collapsible Pole, a multi segment pole that allows one to have a 10’ pole on hand without having to carry such a large ungainly thing all the time.
1,Weapon Black, cut down on the gleam of blades and other metal to reduce the odds of a reflection at a bad time (eases hiding).
1,Magnetic Filings, can be spread on an area to detect magnetic metals, aid in locating a trap or concealed mechanism.
1,Wax Block, for making a quick imprint of a key or seal.
1,Strapping, strong leather strapping to improve tension, tie off tools  when dangling on a wall, or aid in a slow climb (less likely to fall when tied to something).
1,Awl Pick, a lock pick designed to defeat a lock by breaking internal workings.
1,Finger Pick, a tiny pick worn on a fingertip to allow picking of very sensitive locks without risk of dropping a pick.
1,Pin Lamp, a very small candle lamp that only emits a pin point of light meant to illuminate a very small working area.
1,Climber’s Claws, hand-sized rake-like claws to aid climbing.
1,Cat’s Harness, an elaborate leather harness with fittigns and hooks to attach tools and lines to improve “second story” work.
1,Stick Mirror, a tiny mirror on a collapsible metal rod useful for looking through holes and around corners.
1,Oversocks, slipover boots or shows to move more quietly.
